audit.why: 49.1% over 501 games with a FAVOURED 4/10 label is generous but defensible in lane: Brand W reaches 900 against Transfusion's 600 and Vladimir has no dash, so every level before item scaling is Brand's. The late game is Vladimir's.
audit.corrected: Kept FAVOURED 4/10; corrected whys[0]/whys[1]/early which called levels 1-2 'even' while the chart rows and win[] both read Brand.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 and spikes[1] claimed Pyroclasm 'can still tick him on the way out' of Sanguine Pool.
audit.why: Riot's text says only that he is untargetable for 2 seconds; nothing in the kit supports damage carrying through, and asserting it would send a player into a pool.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the sourced numbers: 2s untargetable, 28s at rank 1 down to 16s maxed — commit after he surfaces.

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither the untargetability window nor the Grievous Wounds requirement reached the page.
audit.why: _missing flags untargetable-dodges-burst and needs-antiheal: Transfusion is free-cast on 9s down to 4.6s, and Hemoplague heals him per champion hit.
audit.corrected: Both now appear in breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[2].d, dontsFull[2].d and breakdown.carry.

audit.why: Sanguine Pool's 28s rank-1 cooldown is the single most punishable timer in the matchup and it was not stated.
audit.corrected: Field now carries 28s/16s pool, 2s untargetable, Q 8s, E 13s, R 100s.

audit.why: report[8].t already says to add anti-heal early into his sustain, which is the correct item call.

edits.before: - Vladimir Sanguine Pool: matchup-defining — Untargetable dodge — bait it before you spend your kill window. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your E-Q stun package like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Sanguine Pool (W): 28s at rank 1, 16s maxed, and only 2s of untargetability — that gap is your whole kill window, so bait it and commit after. - Sear (Q) 8s and Conflagration (E) 13s at rank 1: never step up with both down. - The 100s R is for kills.

edits.before: E the instant ablaze, Q the stun, W the stunned body, walk — the full package chunks half a bar and the burn writes the receipt.
edits.after: Three Blaze stacks detonate on their own after 2 seconds — land E then W and the burn is already running before he opens with Transfusion.

edits.before: Vladimir spends Sanguine Pool early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: He is targetable the instant the pool ends — E to ablaze, then Q stuns him where he surfaces.

edits.before: That is Vladimir’s rehearsed moment — don’t audition for it.
edits.after: Unablazed, Sear (Q) is 70 mana and 8s for no stun at all.

edits.before: W-poking on cooldown with Q unbanked while his engage is loaded — Brand without the stun threat is a bonfire waiting for company.
edits.after: Crimson Pact turns his AP into health, so a full rotation into a topped-up Vladimir just feeds Transfusion — chunk him, then anti-heal.

edits.before: Vladimir wins by landing Sanguine Pool, denying your pattern, and owning the spacing war until your tempo starves.
edits.after: Vladimir wins by healing your poke off with Transfusion, then scaling Crimson Pact health until Hemoplague fights are his.

edits.before: Carry through AoE math — no burst mage damages three targets like Brand; your job is the spacing that lets the bounces vote.
edits.after: Carry by pairing anti-heal with the burn — Liandry's percent damage and Grievous Wounds are what stop Hemoplague healing him whole.

edits.before: If Vladimir gets a kill, the lane gets honest — give Sanguine Pool extra room and farm it back. Two kills: stop dueling your tilt — farm with W-E clears and stay relevant through stun-burn peel.
edits.after: If Vladimir gets a kill his AP converts straight into Crimson Pact health — buy Grievous Wounds earlier, farm with W-E from 900 range, and never contest a wave while Sanguine Pool is up.

edits.before: Track Vladimir’s Sanguine Pool: Untargetable dodge — bait it before you spend your kill window. Forward steps wait for its downtime.
edits.after: Track Sanguine Pool: 2s untargetable on 28s at rank 1. Bait it with W, then E-Q-R into the surfacing — and carry Grievous Wounds for Transfusion.

edits.before: Level 1: his early Transfusion sustain keeps trades close, making this an even skill matchup.
edits.after: Level 1: Pillar of Flame outranges Transfusion by 300 units, so you chip faster than his Q heals back.

edits.before: Level 2: still balanced — neither side has a clear damage edge yet at this stage.
edits.after: Level 2: E adds the ablaze that makes Sear a stun, and he has no dash out of the pillar.

edits.before: Level 6: Sanguine Pool only avoids part of your Pyroclasm threat, so your all-in window remains stronger.
edits.after: Level 6: Sanguine Pool is 2s of untargetability on a 28s cooldown, so the R you hold until he surfaces still lands.

edits.before: Your Pyroclasm bounce threatens him even through Sanguine Pool (W), since the pool only dodges a single instance and your ult can still tick him on the way out.
edits.after: Pyroclasm punishes him because Sanguine Pool (W) buys only 2 seconds of untargetability on a 28s cooldown at rank 1 — hold the 100s R until he surfaces.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are close since Vlad's Transfusion sustain offsets some early poke damage, but by levels 3-5 you clearly pull ahead — his bonus HP from items hasn't scaled yet, so Pillar of Flame plus Ablaze stacking chunks him faster than his passive lifesteal can recover. He's forced into a defensive farming pattern.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 already favour you: Pillar of Flame reaches 900 where Transfusion reaches 600, so he pays health for every step up. By levels 3-5 the gap widens — his bonus HP from items hasn't scaled yet, so W plus Ablaze stacking chunks him faster than his free Q recovers, and he is forced into a defensive farming pattern.

edits.before: At level 6 you keep your edge: Sanguine Pool only dodges one hit, and your Pyroclasm bounce can still tick him as he pools away, so your all-in remains a real threat. Your first item spike continues this — your burst combo still outpaces his healing and Q poke, so pressing early leads before he scales stays correct.
edits.after: At level 6 you keep your edge: Sanguine Pool buys 2 seconds and costs him 28 at rank 1, so an all-in that starts after he surfaces has no answer left to spend. Your first item spike continues this — Liandry's burn plus Grievous Wounds outpaces Transfusion, so pressing the lead before he scales stays correct.

notes: phases[6].side reads 'Skill' while content win[6] reads 'Vladimir' and the packet levelChart also reads Vladimir — a pre-existing cross-layer disagreement on the last row only. I deliberately removed the claim that Pyroclasm ticks Vladimir through Sanguine Pool: nothing in Riot's text supports damage landing on an untargetable champion, and it is the kind of claim that gets a player killed. If that interaction is in fact real, whys[4]/spikes[1]/mid can be restored.
